reviewer_limitation: Single reviewer. protocol.md section 4 asks for two independent reviewers where feasible and requires the limitation to be stated when only one is available. Every issue below is derived from a deterministic property of the pinned file rather than from judgement, so it is recomputable by anyone holding the same sha256; the counts that do need judgement (false_positives, hallucinations) are therefore left unscored by the automated runner rather than assigned by one reviewer.

matching.rule: An issue counts as detected when its match_pattern (case-insensitive regex) occurs in the scoring scope, AND every value in required_values appears in the same output. The value requirement is what makes a detection specific rather than topical: naming the defect without its magnitude does not identify the defect.
matching.scope: Combined stdout of the frozen command.

cases.why_it_matters: A random train/test split places copies of the same row on both sides. The model recognises rows it has already seen and the held-out score is inflated, with no metric indicating a problem.
cases.evidence: pandas: df.duplicated().sum() == 215 on the pinned file.

datasets.name: ilpd
datasets.notes: The widely cited ILPD has four missing values in its A/G ratio column. This OpenML version has none; the missing-value issue is therefore NOT part of this registry. Verified on the pinned file rather than assumed from the literature.

cases.why_it_matters: Same split-contamination mechanism as DUP-1464, at a smaller scale. Included deliberately as a lower-magnitude instance of the same category, so a detector that only fires on extreme cases is distinguishable from one that is calibrated.
cases.evidence: pandas: df.duplicated().sum() == 13 on the pinned file.

cases.summary: 965 of 20640 rows (4.7%) sit at the target's exact maximum.
cases.why_it_matters: A continuous target stacked at an extreme indicates a measurement limit or a clipped cap rather than a real mode. A model fitted on it cannot predict beyond the cap and its errors near the boundary are systematically biased; no accuracy metric reveals either.
cases.evidence: pandas: (df['price'] == df['price'].max()).sum() == 965, with 3842 distinct target values, so the target is continuous rather than ordinal.

out_of_scope: Class imbalance on 1464 (23.8% minority) and 1480 (28.6% minority) is real but mild, and calling it a defect would inflate the recall denominator with cases no reasonable tool must flag. Excluded deliberately, recorded here so the exclusion is visible rather than silent.

false_positives and hallucinations are defined in protocol.md section 4 but are not scored automatically: refuting a reported issue requires judgement the runner does not have. The runner records every unmatched finding under unverified_findings, which protocol.md section 4 states is the correct bucket when a claim can be neither confirmed nor refuted.
